missionLead: We treat NYC tech unemployment and nonprofit under-resourcing as one problem: a career-readiness program that matches job-seeking technologists with qualified nonprofits and NGOs that need data and IT help.
missionParagraphs: Entry-level tech job postings in New York City have fallen 49% since 2022 — putting early-career talent at historic risk of tech unemployment while computer science graduates now outnumber open roles. Traditional degrees alone are no longer enough; employers require applied, production-tested AI experience.

At the same time, qualified social workers, under-resourced nonprofits, and grassroots NGOs are priced out of technical talent. We train Data Diplomats and match them directly with these community organizations to solve pressing data and IT challenges through human-centered AI — creating career-ready candidates on one side and resilient community organizations on the other.

values.title: Career-Ready
values.description: Every match is a job-prep studio: real stakeholders, real data, and real constraints — the applied experience the first rung of tech now requires.

values.title: Matched to Mission
values.description: We place candidates with nonprofits and NGOs whose biggest data and IT problems fit their skills, instead of leaving either side to hunt alone.

values.title: Human-Centered AI
values.description: We teach people to use AI in service of communities and under-resourced staff — not as a reason to erase entry-level jobs.

values.title: Growth-Oriented
values.description: We organize first, then ship: relationships, strategy, and narrative around every match so both diplomats and partners grow.

philosophy.title: Organizing Before Coding
philosophy.intro: Before we write a line of code, we organize. Our approach is grounded in the community-organizing tradition of Dr. Marshall Ganz — a Harvard lecturer and veteran organizer of the United Farm Workers and the 2008 Obama campaign — who teaches that lasting social change is built through relationships, not transactions.
philosophy.frameworkDescription: Ganz likens organizing to riding a bicycle: two wheels turning in sync around a shared center of gravity. We use it to structure every cohort and every nonprofit partnership.

pillars.name: Narrative
pillars.description: Public narrative — telling a Story of Self, a Story of Us, and a Story of Now — turns individual values into shared motivation and a clear call to act.

pillars.name: Relationship
pillars.description: Grassroots, one-on-one relationship building is the hub holding everything together — the trust that lets diplomats and nonprofit partners commit to hard work together.

pillars.name: Strategy
pillars.description: Strategy turns resources — volunteer time, technical skill, and data — into the power needed to reach a concrete goal for each nonprofit partner.

philosophy.theoryOfChangeDescription: We treat two problems as one: NYC's collapsing entry-level tech pathway, and grassroots organizations priced out of modern technology. Matching trained Data Diplomats with qualified social workers, under-resourced nonprofits, and NGOs builds career-ready professionals while delivering critical, human-centered data and IT capacity to our communities.

entityNote: Data Diplomats for Nonprofits is a registered 501(c)(3) that runs the Data Diplomats Training Program: career-ready, human-centered AI training that matches candidates with qualified nonprofits and NGOs to deliver pro bono data and IT solutions. Our Impact Unit also provides workshops and consulting for ethical AI in mission-driven organizations.
